We need to consider A's rationality: A also wants to maximize distinct tasks and minimize total cost. So A will anticipate B's choice? They choose simultaneously, but they both want the global optimum. This is a coordination game. The best joint outcome is the pair (T3,T4) in any order. So likely both will aim for that. But there are two symmetric equilibria: (A=T3,B=T4) and (A=T4,B=T3). Both yield optimal total cost. Are there any incentives to deviate? Suppose A chooses T3, expecting B to choose T4. If B deviates to something else, A's outcome may be worse. But A cannot know B's choice. However, both have common interest to achieve the optimal outcome. So any coordination that leads to the optimal outcome is a Nash equilibrium if no unilateral deviation can improve the shared objective (i.e., increase distinct tasks or reduce cost). Thus B should choose either T3 or T4. Which one is better for B individually? Rewards: In row5 (A=T4,B=T3): B reward = 90 (since B did T3 cost 10, reward 100-10=90).
